blocks.content: NITI Aayog serves as a think tank of the Government of India, fostering cooperative federalism through a bottom-up approach.

rows: Empowered to allocate funds to states
No power to allocate funds (handled by Finance Ministry)
States directly included in the Governing Council

items: NITI Aayog does not have the authority to allocate funds; financial resource allocation is handled directly by the Ministry of Finance.
The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.
Planning Commission relied on Five-Year Plans, whereas NITI Aayog works with 3-year Action Agendas, 7-year Medium Term Strategies, and 15-year Vision Documents.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the 65-year-old Planning Commission on January 1, 2015.
Unlike the Planning Commission which followed a top-down model, NITI Aayog operates on a bottom-up approach to foster cooperative federalism.
The Planning Commission had the power to allocate funds to state governments and central ministries, whereas NITI Aayog is an advisory think tank with no financial allocation powers.
The Governing Council of NITI Aayog comprises Chief Ministers of all States and Lt. Governors of Union Territories, ensuring direct state representation.
